sources.note: Nothing. Calls it 'a poorly-attested Munda language, apparently related to or a dialect of Asuri' and states, citing Census 2011 ST-15, that all Majhwars now record Indo-Aryan mother tongues (Chhattisgarhi, Surgujia, Sadri). Cites only Glottolog and the Census.

sources.note: Not applicable: grep for Majhwar/Majhi/Manjhi = 0 hits; the volume does not cover Majhwar (Sonbhadra). No LSI state volume for Chhattisgarh or Madhya Pradesh exists on archive.org.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid page majh1236 'Majhwar' and reference record 304344 (Grierson 1906, hh bibliography).
sources.note: Nothing; bibliographic only. The reference record's lgcode field reads 'Manjhi = Majhwar [mmj]', confirming that the LSI 'So-called Mañjhi' of Raigarh (pp. 145-146) is the sole source behind Glottolog's Majhwar. Glottolog lists no other descriptive reference (n_glottolog_desc_refs = 0).

sources.citation: Grierson, G. A. (ed.) 1906. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. IV: Munda and Dravidian Languages. Calcutta: Office of the Superintendent of Government Printing. Section 'So-called Mañjhi dialect (State Raigarh)', pp. 145-146 (within Kherwari > Asuri, pp. 135-146).
sources.harvard_location: WID Old Widener 3254.1 F; LIN GEN CoPh 5.40; SAN GEN Ud 0010
sources.note: Nothing. The Mañjhi section is a classification note (a form of speech 'between Asuri and Korwa', 'practically extinct', 'extremely corrupt and mixed with Aryan forms and words') plus the opening lines of the Prodigal Son; no Pronunciation or Accent paragraph; the author writes 'It would be waste of time and paper to go further into detail.' Grep of the whole volume: accent statements exist only for Santali (p. 29), Mundari (p. 85, 'same as in Santali') and a Dravidian language (line 27204), none for Mañjhi/Asuri/Korwa.
